title: The Misinformation Effect
coreConcept: Human memory is malleable and reconstructive; post-event misinformation seamlessly incorporates into original memory traces during reconsolidation.

title: Why People Cannot Read Your Mind as Easily as You Think
coreConcept: Your internal physiological state is far more vivid to your nervous system than it will ever appear to an outside observer.
sources: Gilovich et al. (1998), J Pers Soc Psychol

title: The Ben Franklin Effect
coreConcept: Performing a favor for someone increases interpersonal affinity because the brain retroactively rationalizes the favor as evidence of liking.

title: The Invisible Gorilla (Inattentional Blindness)
coreConcept: Intensive focal visual attention selectively filters unattended visual inputs, preventing unexpected stimuli from entering conscious awareness regardless of physical size or salience.

title: The Doorway Effect (Event Horizon Model)
coreConcept: Navigating physical doorways triggers episodic memory event boundaries in the hippocampus, flushing recent working memory to accommodate new environmental contexts.

title: Why Crowds Freeze When Someone Needs Help
coreConcept: In emergencies, personal responsibility divides by the number of witnesses present unless explicitly directed.
sources: Darley & Latané (1968), J Pers Soc Psychol

topic: Ironic Process Theory (The White Bear Problem)
title: Why Trying Not to Think About Something Guarantees You Will
coreConcept: The brain cannot search for what to avoid without first activating the mental representation of what is forbidden.
sources: Wegner et al. (1987), J Pers Soc Psychol
